subject: infra.connect
name: 2Africa Angola branch
milestone: Landing station inaugurated and service switched on 2025-12-13
position_start: Not in service; the cable had berthed but the branch and landing station were still being built
position_end: In service on a US$43m operator-built branch, with 23.6 Tbps of the cable's capacity allocated to Angola, replacing an end-of-life system and one at capacity
note: the incumbent is the only Angolan member of the consortium

subject: infra.connect
name: Digital terrestrial television transition
milestone: Agreement signed August 2025 at about US$10m
position_start: Did not exist as a financed project
position_end: About US$10m of foreign financing modernising transmitters at three sites, motivated partly by disaster-alert broadcasting; no progress or switchover date published since
note: twelve months with nothing on file

subject: infra.connect
name: Domestic submarine cable
milestone: Stated as in preparation at a ministry council 2026-03-26
position_end: A planned domestic cable to interlink the coastal cities and connect a transport corridor to an international system; no route, cost, financier or date published

subject: infra.connect
name: Enterprise 5G service
position_start: Phase-one technical specifications being finalised, not commercially launched
position_end: Commercially launched in Cabinda, with Luanda at over 70% city coverage, about US$20m budgeted and every provincial capital targeted by 2027
note: enterprise connectivity, not consumer mobile, and the throughput figures are the operator's own

subject: infra.connect
name: Equiano capacity through Namibia
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The state operator to receive an initial 1.0 Tbps of dedicated capacity through a Namibian landing, with an option to assume ownership; design, testing, commissioning and handover still to run
note: Angola reaches this cable only indirectly

subject: infra.connect
name: Fifth-generation standalone network
milestone: Trial standalone data call completed in a live environment
position_start: Core transformation completed and a standalone trial call done, with no commercial launch
position_end: Unchanged; no held source records a commercial standalone launch date
note: a vendor release

subject: infra.connect
name: Low-orbit satellite licence
position_start: A 15-year licence granted in June 2025 with a Luanda ground station, first and only licensed low-orbit operator, no commercial offtake on file
position_end: Licence held and now commercially deployed through a multi-year capacity agreement with a local provider

subject: infra.connect
name: National broadband network
milestone: Specific loan agreement signed October 2023 at about US$249m
position_start: Financed and active, with no delivery milestone published
position_end: Financed and active, still with no delivery milestone
note: a Chinese concessional loan with no progress report on file at either end

subject: infra.connect
name: National terrestrial fibre length
milestone: No authoritative series; five official statements run non-monotonic
position_start: Already inconsistent at 22,000 km in 2023, itself an older figure, against a recurring 2,000 km annual increment
position_end: 22,000 km in 2023, 20,000 in October 2025, 30,000 in November 2025, 22,000 in April 2026 and 28,000 in June 2026; the wiki asserts no current national figure
note: the regulator's annual statistical report that would settle it was dropped as unobtainable

subject: infra.connect
name: Rural roaming and infrastructure-sharing programme
milestone: A tower commissioned in Moxico June 2026
position_end: National roaming and infrastructure sharing with shared towers, solar power and satellite backhaul, extending voice and data to remote areas
note: no national site count, budget or target published

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink licence
milestone: Licensing process open since 2024 and unresolved
position_start: Unlicensed, with the ministry saying only that negotiations were continuing
position_end: Unlicensed; a secretary of state says only that the process is under way, and the regulator is still working out how to fit low-orbit operators into a regime written for terrestrial networks
note: sixteen months of identical status is the finding

subject: infra.store
name: Commercial data centre
position_start: Did not exist; the country had no Tier III commercial data centre
position_end: Operating at up to 3 MW and more than 800 racks over 19,000 square metres on US$30m, near the cable landings, with a plan to exceed 7 MW within five years
sources: 2025-10-02 Raxio Opens Angola's Largest Data Centre in Landmark 30 Million Expansion|2026-07-23-raxio-afr-ix-data-centres-angola-mozambique
note: the group contracted six times as much power in the first half of 2026 as a year earlier

subject: infra.store
name: Government data centre
position_start: Under construction at about 75% complete, operation expected in the first half of 2026
position_end: Operating at 6,225 square metres, Tier III design, 208 racks and 1,040 kW live in a modular design of about 336-rack capacity, reported at about US$89m
sources: 2026-04-28-pr-inaugura-novo-centro-de-dados-do-governo|2025-11-14 Angola Nears Completion of National Data Center, Set for 2026 Launch
note: two accounts give US$89m and about US$90m, and no kwanza original is published

subject: infra.store
name: National cloud
milestone: Launched with the government data centre 2026-04-28
position_start: First stone laid September 2025, with a migration mandate stated and nothing yet to migrate onto
position_end: A unified government cloud in operation under a progressive and mandatory migration of public services, framed as repatriating passports and education certificates from foreign platforms
sources: 2026-04-28-centro-de-dados-do-governo-soberania-digital|2025-09-10 Angola advances technological development for digital transformation
note: no source records how much has actually migrated

subject: infra.store
name: Second commercial data centre project
milestone: Announced 2023-06-27 with a US$31m facility in November 2023
position_start: Announced as the country's first Tier IV facility at over 10 MW and 2,000 racks, financed but not built
position_end: Unchanged; no source since 2023 and no completion date was ever stated
sources: 2023-06-27 Paratus to build third Angola data center (DC3, Tier IV)
note: three years of silence on the only Tier IV project in the country

subject: infra.energy
name: Household access to electricity
position_start: 31.9% of households in the 2014 census
position_end: 48.6% of households at the 2024 census reference date, 68.9% urban and 8.5% rural
sources: 2025-11-20-ine-angola-censo-2024-relatorio-sintese-resultados-definitivos|2023-07-04 AD664 - Lack of grid access plagues most rural residents in Angola
note: the physical floor under every named object in this section

subject: infra.energy
name: Power Sector Action Plan electrification target
milestone: Target year passed with no published outturn
position_start: A target of 60% electrification by 2025, from 47% in 2020, still open
position_end: The target year passed, with the only later dated measure a different one and no electrification rate published since the 2020 baseline
sources: 2023-07-04 AD664 - Lack of grid access plagues most rural residents in Angola|2025-11-20-ine-angola-censo-2024-relatorio-sintese-resultados-definitivos

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Critical national infrastructure designation
position_start: None published
position_end: Named analysts argued after a national mobile outage that telecommunications should be designated critical alongside power and water; the operator dates the attack to the early hours of 2026-07-28 and states that voice, messaging, mobile data, internet access and third-party services over its network were restored on 2026-08-05, nine days later; no instrument exists, and the bill that would supply the designation is still a proposal
note: enactment of the cybersecurity law, or a standalone decree, would settle it

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cyber-security appropriation
position_start: Kz 70.5bn in the 2025 budget, about US$76.4m at the source's stated rate
position_end: Kz 32.3bn in the 2026 budget, about US$35m, still the third-largest item inside the communications programme
note: read at draft stage before enactment

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cybersecurity fund
milestone: Presupposed by the cyber centre's statute, established by nothing on file
position_end: The statute splits the centre's receipts three ways including a share to a cybersecurity fund, which is created and governed by no instrument the wiki holds
note: a constitutive decree would settle it

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Citizen-database interoperability commission
milestone: A presidential decree created an interministerial commission 2026-06-08
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A commission to stabilise civil-identification and adult-citizen database interoperability, biometrically de-duplicate, update residence and consolidate the electoral base, with a US$275m supplementary credit
note: no technical standard, interface or completion date is on file

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Logistics single window
milestone: Phase one expected between the second half of 2026 and the first half of 2027
position_start: Did not exist; the port, foreign-trade and customs platforms ran separately
position_end: An integrated ecosystem to absorb three separate agency platforms into one, framed explicitly as a formalisation and tax-base instrument rather than trade facilitation
note: a board communique is the only source; no instrument, budget or vendor named

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Public digital infrastructure contract
position_start: Did not exist; no national interoperability platform in service
position_end: US$150m over a twelve-month execution period for a secure-zone critical-computing component hosting the interoperability platform, key-based electronic signatures, digital identity and structured cybersecurity; in execution from 2026-07-31, financed under Despacho Presidencial n.º 38/26 and inscribed in the 2026 public investment programme
note: a sole-referenced state technology award under a presidential order, procurement route unstated

subject: dpi.id
name: At-home identity-card service
milestone: Launched 2026-07-28, first phase in one province only
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Kz 250,000 for at-home processing and Kz 10,000 for at-home delivery alone, on a 48-hour issuance target, with requests through a web portal and a messaging number
note: the ministry called the fee a product of exclusivity, and no ministry publication naming the portal is on file

subject: dpi.id
name: Biometric electronic passport
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Issued across all 21 provinces by end-March 2026 and to the diaspora from May 2026
note: no issuance volume or backlog figure published

subject: dpi.id
name: Civil and criminal identification bill
milestone: Approved by the Council of Ministers 2026-04-29
position_start: Did not exist; voter cards, driving licences and passports accepted as substitutes
position_end: Would make the identity card the only valid document for banking, telecoms, school enrolment, property registration and contracts, and set the country's first dedicated identity-data-processing regime
note: no parliamentary stage recorded since April 2026

subject: dpi.id
name: Identity card coverage
position_start: No national coverage figure published; a 2023 diagnostic states only that the country is far from universal coverage
position_end: 52.4% of the population aged five and over hold the card, 63% urban against 30.9% rural, leaving 14.9m people undocumented
note: the movement is in measurement, not in coverage

subject: dpi.id
name: National identity card
milestone: Issuing on a foreign-built platform since 2017
position_start: In issue, one of several accepted identity documents, coverage unmeasured
position_end: In issue nationwide and generated from the birth record by system interoperability, with coverage now measured and sole-identity status pending in a 2026 bill
note: the credential is unchanged; what moved is its measurement and its proposed legal monopoly

subject: dpi.id
name: Single digital identity
milestone: Named as a component of the public digital infrastructure contract
position_start: Named as a workstream in the 2024 World Bank loan agreement, nothing built
position_end: A component of the US$150m build, with no design, standard, pilot or launch date on file
note: distinct from the identity card, and the base carries no specification of what it is

subject: dpi.pay
name: Financial inclusion rate
milestone: Scorecard given by a state minister 2026-07-09
position_end: 51.7% at the first quarter of 2026 against a 65% target for 2027, with banking at 32% or 5.7m people and mobile and digital payments up about 56% year on year
note: the strategy launched in December 2025 and no pre-strategy baseline figure is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Instant payment scheme
position_start: 35m transfers and Kz 590bn over 2025 across 22 banking and non-banking institutions
position_end: Wallet-led and concentrated, with the largest wallet at 52.2% of transfers, more than 12.3m registered accounts and about 24.8m active payment keys, and 66.4% of transfers under Kz 10,000
note: the base holds no launch date and no figure dated before 2025

subject: dpi.pay
name: Kwanza as a regional settlement currency
milestone: Formally introduced by the two central-bank governors 2026-07-27
position_start: Not a settlement currency; the regional system had cleared in one currency since 2013
position_end: The second settlement currency in the system's history, against 2025 trade and interbank flows with the other fourteen member states of about US$3.77bn across nine currencies

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payments messaging standard migration
position_end: Domestic payments migrated to the international messaging standard across the switch, the exchange and the real-time settlement participants
note: only the completion is dated; no programme start, scope document or cost is held

subject: dpi.registry
name: Birth registration coverage
position_start: 53.5% overall and 24.8% for children aged nought to four in the 2014 census
position_end: 63.0% overall and only 39.2% among children aged nought to four at the 2024 census reference date
note: the pipeline feeding the identity card is under-registering the newest cohort fastest

subject: dpi.registry
name: Birth registration in maternity wards
milestone: Launched in one province 2026-03-04, running there since October 2025
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Registry posts in maternity wards so newborns leave registered and issued a first identity card, foreign-funded with UN support
sources: 2026-03-04-zaire-inicia-registo-de-recem-nascidos-na-maternidade|2025-11-17 Angola begins issuance of ID cards to newborns
note: no national rollout map or registration count published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Civil-registration post rehabilitation
position_start: A US$250m local-governance project across eight provinces and 53 municipalities
position_end: Eleven birth-registration posts rehabilitated in one province and thirteen in another, with mass campaigns reaching several thousand people
note: only two provinces have published delivery counts

subject: dpi.registry
name: Deconcentrated identity-card printing
position_start: Did not exist; every card printed at a single national production centre
position_end: All 21 provinces print locally, with two to three printers per province planned and a 24-to-48-hour issuance target; one province reports issuance under 24 hours against one to two weeks before
note: printing decentralisation only; enrolment and biometric capture are untouched

subject: dpi.registry
name: Electoral register proof-of-life operation
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: 254 of a planned 634 counters live across all 21 provinces and the diaspora, with 10,747 field workers against a target universe of 16,707,455 citizens; undocumented citizens must first obtain an identity card
note: no enrolment figure has been published since it opened

subject: dpi.registry
name: Private credit information centres
milestone: No licensing instrument, operator or start date on file
position_end: The data-protection agency, working with the International Finance Corporation, explained the centres, their personal-data safeguards and their expected economic effect to journalists on 2026-08-05; no licensing instrument, named operator or start date is on file
note: an APD or central-bank licensing instrument, or a named operating centre, would settle it

subject: dpi.registry
name: Property-legalisation platform
milestone: A target of 40,000 properties legalised by end-2026 set 2026-04-17
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A digital platform linking the cadastre, the tax authority and the property registry, aimed at cutting duplication and enabling mortgage access
note: no progress figure against the target has been published since April 2026

subject: dpi.registry
name: Single social register
milestone: Launched in Luanda in the week ending 2026-07-25
position_start: Did not exist; social-transfer targeting rested on one programme's registry alone
position_end: A single national social registry to map vulnerable households and act as the centralised database directing social supports
note: no enrolment target, data-protection basis, interoperability plan or governing instrument stated at launch

subject: dpi.registry
name: Uncollected identity cards
milestone: Civic campaign launched enlisting churches and traditional authorities
position_end: More than 120,000 issued cards awaiting collection at identification posts nationwide
note: the first such figure the base holds, with no prior series to read it against

subject: dpi.mis
name: Education and research network
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A national education and research network presented alongside an executive roadmap for higher-education digital transformation
note: no connected institutions, capacity, funding or operating date stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: Vaccination registry
milestone: In use across all national vaccination campaigns
position_start: In use for real-time individual vaccination registration
position_end: Used in all national campaigns, with interoperability to the national health information system under development
note: a secretary of state's conference remarks are the only source; no coverage or record count

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Count of public services available online
position_end: The transition agenda counts projects, not services
note: a published service catalogue or a completion report would settle it

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Digital transition agenda
position_start: 214 structuring projects
position_end: 218 structuring projects across six objectives and seven axes, coordinated by a modernisation institute under the presidency
note: the project count is the only published progress metric, and nothing states how many are complete

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Mandatory electronic invoicing
position_start: Decreed but not in force, with the start date postponed
position_end: Mandatory for large taxpayers and state suppliers, extending to all registered taxpayers within twelve months, on certified software with real-time transmission and a standard audit format; more than 500 packages registered and 21 certified
note: no compliance or invoice-volume figure since the mandate took effect

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Public key infrastructure
milestone: Contracted inside the public digital infrastructure build
position_start: Announced in June 2025 as a ministerial intention, nothing contracted and no legal basis
position_end: Contracted as a component of the US$150m project, with the tax authority already running mandatory electronic invoicing on it in practice
note: the trust layer is being built ahead of the law that would govern it

subject: gov.legislate
name: Artificial intelligence bill
milestone: Draft published for public consultation September 2025
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: An 86-article draft in nine chapters out for public consultation, with a single critical-AI category carrying registration, security-risk assessment and emergency-response duties rather than a tiered risk pyramid, extraterritorial reach over activity abroad affecting Angolan interests, a right to explanation and to refuse AI-based decisions, criminal and strict civil liability, and no repeal of existing legislation; no tabling, committee stage or vote on record
sources: 2025-09-01-angola-proposta-de-lei-inteligencia-artificial|2025-12-29 Review of Angola's Proposed Law on Artificial Intelligence
note: the draft text is now held; it defers military AI to a separate instrument and excludes scientific research and purely personal use

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybersecurity bill
milestone: Joint committee report approved in detail 2026-08-07
position_start: No cybersecurity law in force, and nothing held on a bill
position_end: Approved in detail in joint committee by 23 votes to none with 10 abstentions, with the final global vote set for 2026-08-13; fines set as multiples of the national minimum wage, from 7 to 70 for individuals and 70 to 150 for legal persons on minor infractions up to 150 to 450 and 2,000 to 4,000 on very serious ones; no final vote, no promulgation, no gazette number and no entry into force
note: a July 2026 suspension over drafting defects is the prior value, not a competing one

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital government bill
position_start: No framework law; sector rules dispersed since 1997
position_end: In public consultation, framed expressly around ending legislative dispersion and keeping the digital law and the data-protection law in step
note: no draft text and no tabling date held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic signature and certification regime
position_start: A public-key and time-stamp infrastructure announced by the ministry with no legislation, date or location
position_end: Authorisation granted to the President, valid 90 days after publication of the enabling law; the substantive text will be an executive instrument defining an accrediting authority, a root certification entity and the evidential weight of a signature
note: grounded on the insufficiency of two 2011 instruments

subject: gov.legislate
name: National cybersecurity centre
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A public institute with legal personality and administrative and financial autonomy, carrying regulatory, supervisory, inspection and sanctioning powers, an internal emergency response team and a round-the-clock operations department, retaining 30% of the fines it levies
note: no source records it exercising any power or naming a director general

subject: gov.legislate
name: Online falsehoods law
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: In force since 6 August 2026; fines 200-400 minimum wages, prison terms of 3 years for simple publication, 3-8 years for incitement or reputation harm, up to 10 years where it compromises electoral processes or state security; jurist Jaime Domingos (Mudei) calls the definition too vague ahead of the August 2027 election; NGOs plan a legal challenge with the bar association
note: no enforcement action under it anywhere in the country is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Startups law
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Passed, with a legal definition of a startup at an annual revenue ceiling of about US$3.5m and no minimum threshold, admitting pre-revenue ventures
note: promulgation and gazette number not held

subject: gov.policy
name: National artificial intelligence strategy
milestone: A readiness assessment delivered to the ministry names its absence
position_end: Not published; the assessment identifies the absence of a specific instrument as the central gap and is to serve as the base for policy
note: no adoption date, drafting body or timetable on record

subject: gov.policy
name: National cybersecurity council
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Created as a consultative body chaired by the President; no source records it convening and no membership list is on file

subject: gov.policy
name: National cybersecurity strategy
position_start: None published
position_end: In force, approved in Council of Ministers in October 2025 and signed in November, with six strategic objectives and a two-phase legislative reform whose first phase is the bill

subject: gov.regional
name: Bilateral memorandum with a Lusophone regulator
milestone: Signed at a global privacy assembly 2025-09-18
position_start: No bilateral with any non-African regulator held
position_end: In force, providing mutual assistance and technical, regulatory and supervisory cooperation
note: a stated intention to conclude a similar arrangement elsewhere is unevidenced

subject: gov.standards
name: Artificial intelligence readiness score
milestone: Preliminary findings presented to the ministry 2026-06-30
position_end: 50.9% of indicators fully ready, 32.7% partially ready and 16% insufficient, with data governance at 47 out of 100 and science-workforce availability at about 12%
note: the widely quoted higher figure is the first two bands added together, not a readiness score

subject: gov.protect
name: Amendment opening electoral data
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Rejected, leaving the citizen databases and the electoral registers closed to parties and citizens
note: had cleared committee in April 2026; resolved for privacy over electoral transparency

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection agency
milestone: Organic statute gazetted 2016-10-10; board of three appointed 2019-09-06
position_start: Constituted and sanctioning under the superintendence of the telecommunications minister, with a 2024 wave that included the incumbent telecoms operator
position_end: In operation, sanctioning, and now the country's regional data-governance convener, with three of the seven board seats filled, every member removable by presidential decree at any time and without stated grounds, and own revenue from the fines it levies and the fees it charges, of which it retains 60% — revenue onto which a 2021 pay decree moved most of each board member's salary from May 2024
sources: 2026-06-26-apd-aplica-multas-milionarias-crescer-tech-fast-digital-center|2016-10-10-angola-decreto-presidencial-214-16-estatuto-organico-apd|2019-09-06-angola-decreto-presidencial-277-19-nomeacao-conselho-administracao-apd|2021-03-10-angola-decreto-presidencial-60-21-regulamento-taxas-apd|2021-05-25-angola-decreto-presidencial-126-21-estatuto-remuneratorio-apd|2024-08-10 Angola - Dados Pessoais e Ciber-seguranca (APD enforcement)
note: the four seats the National Assembly and the judiciary elect are not established as ever having been filled

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection law
position_start: In force since 2011, with consent and notification duties, sensitive-data limits and transfer approvals, and prior authorisation dispensed with wherever the processing derives from a statute or decree
position_end: In force and unamended, with fines of USD 75,000 to 150,000 and USD 65,000 to 130,000 on individuals, trebled for legal persons and materially cumulated across concurrent contraventions; article 35(6) substitutes a statute or decree for the regulator's authorisation, article 24 does the same for database interconnection, and article 4(2)(a) puts processing under state-secrecy, state-security and judicial-secrecy rules outside the law altogether
sources: 2011-06-17-angola-lei-22-11-proteccao-de-dados-pessoais|2026-07-29-angola-idea-forum-recommends-policy-harmonisation|2011-09-19 Angola Passes Personal Data Protection Law (Law 22-11)
note: a legal person's ceiling is USD 450,000; the figure the wiki previously carried was the individual ceiling

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection law revision
position_end: Consultation closed on a revision adding a data-protection officer duty for high-volume processors, stronger oversight and sanction mechanisms, and redenominating fines into local currency; due at the Council of Ministers then the National Assembly
note: no draft text held

subject: gov.protect
name: Judicial oversight regime for state surveillance
status: Implemented, prosecutorial rather than judicial authorisation
position_start: In force since April 2020: cellular location and electronic surveillance authorised in writing by the Ministério Público where the premises are private or restricted, and by the head of the police body in urgent cases with notice to the prosecutor within 72 hours
position_end: Unchanged; no judicial warrant is required at any stage, execution runs 90 days renewable once for cellular location and successively for electronic surveillance until instruction closes, private persons and businesses must open their own video-surveillance systems to the criminal police in real time or deferred, and the data-protection authority is given knowledge and monitoring of the resulting police database rather than authorisation
sources: 2020-04-23-angola-lei-11-20-vigilancia-electronica|2026-02-26-sinse-adquiriu-spyware-predator-para-espiar-jornalista|2025-10-08 Data protection and cybersecurity laws in Angola (CMS guide)
note: the only evidence of use on file is a forensic confirmation that an intelligence service acquired commercial spyware and that it infected a journalist's phone

subject: gov.protect
name: Published data-protection fines
position_start: A 2024 sanctions wave published, with no totals held
position_end: Over Kz 600m across two firms, following two earlier fines divulged in September 2025
sources: 2026-06-26-apd-aplica-multas-milionarias-crescer-tech-fast-digital-center|2024-08-10 Angola - Dados Pessoais e Ciber-seguranca (APD enforcement)
note: deliberation texts and deliberation dates are not published

subject: gov.protect
name: Video-surveillance licensing regime
position_start: In force since December 2021: installations licensed by the minister responsible for public security on an application filed with the National Police, carrying a prior opinion of the data-protection authority, with the police holding the national database of installed systems and carrying out inspection
position_end: Unchanged; recordings are erased at 30 days unless a criminal-police or judicial body has requested them, technical specification is mandated down to the camera housing and encryption, and authorisation fees are split 40% to the State, 35% to the National Police and 25% to the data-protection authority, with fines split 40% Treasury, 40% police and 20% authority
note: implements Lei n.º 2/20 and names the Centro Integrado de Segurança Pública as the public-security integration body

subject: include.divides
name: Commercial satellite access programme
milestone: First regulator licence to a startup 2026-07-02
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A commercial access hub opened in December 2025, 37 firms in the integration process by April 2026, and a first startup licensed to resell access
note: bandwidth, pricing and operator access terms remain undisclosed

subject: include.divides
name: Satellite connectivity programme
position_end: Six universities and more than 300 localities where mobile operators are absent, with 20,000 students stated, against 27 locations and about 366,000 citizens stated to a UN body in November 2025
note: the white-space leg connected 3,972 students at two schools, a different measure

subject: include.divides
name: Universal service fund
status: Implemented, no accounts or disbursement on record
position_start: On statute since 2010 and funded by 1% of telecom operators' gross revenue, with no accounts published
position_end: Unchanged; the fund and its 1% levy remain on statute, it may make non-repayable grants for non-commercial universal-service expansion but is barred from subsidising operating costs, and no accounts, grant or disbursement have been published for any year
note: required by article 15 of Lei n.º 8/01; whether 1% is still the rate in force is not established

subject: include.access
name: Bancarisation rate
milestone: Ministerial statement to a regional meeting
position_start: No official rate held; a 2023 industry figure put roughly half of the population unbanked
position_end: About 32% of the population, 5.7 million citizens, in the banking system, targeting 36% and about eight million by 2027
sources: 2026-07-09-nova-etapa-estrategia-nacional-de-inclusao-financeira|2023-06-26 Mobile Money in Angola - How Afrimoney is paving the way
note: the 2023 and 2026 figures use different bases and are not a series

subject: include.access
name: Cash-transfer programme
